Aggressive terms can create losses, guarantees or uncapped liability before mobilisation; mitigated through formal bid/no-bid approval, legal/commercial review, liability caps, milestones and termination rights.
Large multi-location or EPC scopes can exceed the company's current organisational capacity; addressed through phased mobilisation, a project management office and earned-milestone reporting.

The company depends on partners for technical capability, licences, assets and delivery in adjacencies such as infrastructure, renewable, EV and defence; partner failure, withdrawal or underperformance transfers directly to VLEG where it carries customer liability.

Government and EPC contracts commonly require upfront mobilisation funding, performance guarantees and slow certification before payment; a single large award can absorb a disproportionate share of the company's resources.
Legacy credentials may not meet contemporary cloud, API, geospatial, AI or security requirements demanded by current tenders.

Public procurement, listing, tax, defence, environmental and labour obligations are complex and change frequently; inherited GST litigation and expected credit loss were identified as key audit matters by the statutory auditor.

As a small, rebuilding organisation, VLEG depends heavily on a few leaders and specialists (7 permanent employees as of 31 March 2026), addressed through succession planning, delegation and retention of critical-capability individuals.
